post.description:
Shared OTP verification. The `purpose` you send decides which flow runs and which response shape you get back.

### `customer_auth` — from `POST /auth/customer/send-otp`
Returns `access_token`, `refresh_token`, `user_id` and `is_profile_completed`.

- **`is_profile_completed = 0`** → redirect to **Complete Profile** (`POST /customers/profile/complete`)
- **`is_profile_completed = 1`** → redirect to **Home**

### `driver_auth` — from `POST /auth/driver/send-otp`
Used by **both** employee and marketplace drivers. Branch on `is_registered`:

- **`is_registered: true`** → a full session (`access_token` + `refresh_token`) is issued alongside a `user` object, exactly as `customer_auth` does. It carries the driver profile plus `driver_type` (`employee` or `marketplace`) and the read-only `current_vehicle`, so the app can render the dashboard without a second call. `driver_type` is also returned at the top level, and the same object is repeated as `driver` for clients written against the earlier shape. Go to the dashboard.
- **`is_registered: false`** → an `access_token` is still returned, but it is a **60-minute signup token, not a session**: it carries the number this OTP just proved and is accepted only by the `/drivers/signup*` endpoints. Send it as the Bearer token there; every other driver endpoint rejects it with 401. `registration_status` says where the driver is:
  - `null` — never applied → start onboarding, `POST /drivers/signup`
  - `pending` — under review → account-status screen, poll `GET /drivers/signup/status`
  - `rejected` — re-upload the flagged documents, then the application returns to review

A driver only receives a real session **after an admin approves** their application — that response is the one that also carries `refresh_token` and a `driver` object.

### `password_reset` — from `POST /auth/forgot-password`
Returns a short-lived `reset_token` for `POST /auth/reset-password`.

Max 3 incorrect attempts before the OTP is invalidated — call the relevant `send-otp` again for a fresh code. In non-production, `9999` is accepted for any purpose.

Emails the enquiry to the team. Nothing is stored — this is a contact channel, not a support ticket, so it does not appear under `/support/tickets`.

`first_name`, `last_name`, `email`, `subject` and `message` are required; `phone`, `preferred_date` and `passengers` are optional and may be omitted or sent blank.

`subject` is the selected "How can we help?" option and is forwarded as sent, so the site can change its option list without a backend change.

**Blank optionals are accepted.** A web form posts untouched inputs as `""`; `phone`, `preferred_date` and `passengers` treat an empty string the same as omitting the field.

**A 201 means the email was accepted by the mail server, not merely queued.** If the send fails the endpoint returns 500 and the visitor should be told their message did not get through — never show a success screen on a non-201.

post.description:
Takes the same fare inputs as `POST /public/bookings/calculate-fare`, plus contact details, a requested pickup time, and an optional guest passenger.

1. Finds an existing customer by `phone`, or creates a new customer account if none exists.
2. Creates a real, pending booking under that customer (same as the authenticated booking flow).
3. Initiates a real payment intention with whichever gateway `DEFAULT_PAYMENT_GATEWAY` selects, and returns it under `payment`. For Paymob, `payment.client_secret` + `payment.public_key` are populated — pass both to the Paymob web SDK to process payment directly from the website. For every gateway, `payment.checkout_url` is a ready-to-use link to the provider's hosted checkout page (redirect the browser there, or open it in an iframe) if you'd rather not integrate an SDK directly. For a PayTabs checkout, once the customer returns from the hosted page, use `POST /public/bookings/manual-booking/:id/confirm-payment` with the `checkout_id` (tran_ref) for a synchronous, server-verified confirmation instead of waiting on the webhook.

The notification email to the booking team is sent only after the gateway confirms the payment succeeded (via its server-to-server webhook, or via confirm-payment for PayTabs) — it is NOT sent by this endpoint. If payment is never completed, no email is sent, but the booking and customer records this call created still exist (payment_status stays `pending`).

The response also includes `auth_token` — a short-lived (24h) token scoped to this one booking, since this customer has no login session. After redirecting back from the gateway's checkout, present it as a Bearer token to `GET /public/bookings/manual-booking/:id/status` (or the confirm-payment endpoint above, for PayTabs) to poll or confirm whether payment succeeded.

After the customer finishes the hosted checkout, the browser is redirected to `success_url` if the payment succeeded, or `fail_url` otherwise (rejected, cancelled, still pending, etc.) — `booking_id` and a fresh `auth_token` are appended to whichever URL is used as query params.

vehicle_id.description: Optional. Must belong to vehicle_class_id. Prices using this vehicle's own rate overrides where set, falling back to the class rate for anything unset. Also recorded on the created booking.

scheduled_datetime.description: Requested pickup date/time. The date/time fields are always read as Asia/Riyadh local time — any offset or "Z" suffix in the string is ignored. The example above is read as 2:30pm Riyadh time.

phone.description: Customer phone number — used to find or create the customer account

guest.description: Optional guest passenger, if this booking is for someone other than the contact above

success_url.description: Redirect target after a successful payment — booking_id and auth_token are appended as query params

fail_url.description: Redirect target if payment fails, is cancelled, or is not completed — booking_id and auth_token are appended as query params

post.description:
Fetches flight schedule data from aviationstack's flightsFuture endpoint and returns it in our own response shape. No authentication required.

Unlike a live/historical flight tracker, this only covers **upcoming** dates — same-day or past flights are not available here.

Search is by **airport + direction + date**, not by flight number directly — `airport_iata` (default `RUH`) and `direction` (default `arrival`) select which airport schedule to search, and the result is filtered down to `flight_number` server-side. A flight can match more than once (e.g. it also appears under a codeshare number), so `flights` is always an array and `count` reports how many matched.

Responses are cached for 6 hours per flight number + date + airport + direction, since the upstream plan is metered; `cached` indicates whether the result came from that cache.

email.description: "Email address" — required. Where the team will reply.

phone.description: "Phone Number" — optional. Digits with optional +, spaces, brackets and hyphens, 7–20 characters. Send `""` or omit if not provided.

subject.description: The selected "How can we help?" option. Free-form — the site owns the option list, so the label is stored and forwarded exactly as sent.

preferred_date.description: "Preferred Date" — optional, `YYYY-MM-DD`. Shown in the email formatted for Riyadh time. Send `""` or omit if not provided.

passengers.description: "Passengers" — optional, 1–50. Accepts a number or a numeric string; `""` and `0` are treated as not provided.

message.example: I need an airport pickup for four people on 1 October.
message.description: "Message" — required. Line breaks are preserved in the email.

reason.example: Plans changed, no longer need the ride

flight_number.description: IATA flight number — 2–3 character carrier code plus 1–4 digits, with an optional trailing letter. Whitespace is stripped and the value is upper-cased before lookup.

flight_date.description: Flight date in YYYY-MM-DD format. Schedules come from the flightsFuture endpoint, which covers upcoming dates only — it does not carry same-day or historical data.

airport_iata.description: 3-letter IATA code of the airport to search. Defaults to Riyadh (RUH) — the airport this app is built around — but any airport can be passed for a booking that starts or ends elsewhere.

direction.description: Whether the flight is arriving at or departing from `airport_iata`. Defaults to `arrival` — the common case for airport-pickup bookings.
